steps.title: Send the connected person through GitLab consent and verify the callback state
steps.detail: Redirect the user to the documented authorization endpoint with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, state, and scope=read_api. The user approves on GitLab. Verify the returned state matches the value generated before redirect, then capture the returned code. This is an unexecuted user action; do not fabricate a code.
steps.doneWhen: Callback returns a code and a state equal to the generated state value.

https://example.com/oauth/redirect?code=1234567890&state=STATE With the authorization code returned from the previous request (shown as

fields: APP_ID: from the registered application

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Exchange the returned code at the token endpoint using grant_type=authorization_code with client_id, client_secret, code and redirect_uri matching the authorization request. Store access_token and refresh_token. Expected output is JSON with access_token, token_type bearer, expires_in, refresh_token. This is an unexecuted authorization step.
steps.doneWhen: Token response contains access_token and refresh_token.

steps.title: Read the first page of project issue titles
steps.detail: Call the project issues list with the bearer token and per_page=100. Read the title property of each element of the returned JSON array (the response is a top-level array; $[].title). Expected output: a JSON array of issue objects with title strings. Boundary check: a nonexistent project ID only tests absence; use a project the user is permitted to access and confirm no create/update/delete calls are made.
steps.doneWhen: HTTP 200 with a JSON array; each element has a title string.
